params.body:
## Why

On staging, `stocklist:smoke whatsapp --whatsapp-to=+32...` reported `✗ whatsapp geen bericht-id` while the message was actually delivered and Meta had answered with a message id. `WhatsAppService::send()` wraps Meta's answer as `['status' => ..., 'data' => ...]`, but the check looked for `messages.0.id` at the top level, where it can never be. A smoke test that calls a success a failure is worse than no smoke test.

The mail line had the opposite problem: it only proved that a mailer was configured, never that a message can leave the building. There was no way to send one real mail to a chosen address, the way `--whatsapp-to` does for WhatsApp.

## What

- `checkWhatsapp()` reads the id from `data.messages.0.id`, prints it truncated to 24 characters, and fails only when Meta really refused: a non-2xx status, an `error` key in the answer, or a 2xx answer without a message id. The three cases print what came back instead of a raw dump of the envelope.
- New option `--mail-to=<address>`, in the same spirit as `--whatsapp-to`. Without it nothing is sent and the line reports the configuration: mailer, host, from address, and whether the outbound way is open or sealed. With it one message goes to that address and the line says what the transport did with it, plus the message id when there is one. When `APP_DEBUG` is true the line warns that `Mail::alwaysTo` in `AppServiceProvider` redirects everything, so the operator understands why the mail landed elsewhere.
- `--whatsapp-to` or `--mail-to` on their own now select their check, instead of running into "Geef een dienst op".
- New `App\Mail\SmokeTestMail`: one line of text, no view, no model. Deliberately a Mailable and not `Mail::raw()`, because `MailFake::raw()` records nothing, so a test could not check who was mailed.

## How the seal is respected

Mail is not in `Outbound::services()`; it is not gated per service but by `Outbound::seal()`, which sets `mail.default` to `log` outside production (point 1 of the seal). So this check adds no switch of its own: it sends through the mailer the seal already chose and reports which way out that was. Outside production that is the log file, and the line says so. WhatsApp keeps its own gate, `Outbound::impact('whatsapp')`, unchanged.

No address or phone number is in the repo; both are command-line arguments only.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='IntegrationSmoke|WhatsApp|Smoke|Mail'`: 135 tests, 211 assertions, green, against a local MySQL loaded as CI does.
- New tests: the Graph API success envelope (id read and truncated), a Meta error payload on HTTP 400, a 2xx answer without a message id, mail without an address (nothing sent, configuration reported), mail with an address (`Mail::fake()`, `hasTo`), and the log/`APP_DEBUG` wording.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `CUTOVER.md` describe the new option.
params.title: Smoke: WhatsApp success is success, and a real mail check
